    • FlowrAnalyzerBuilder

    Class FlowrAnalyzerBuilder

    Builder for the FlowrAnalyzer, use it to configure all analysis aspects before creating the analyzer instance with .build() or .buildSync().

    You can add new files and folders to analyze using the .addRequest() method on the resulting analyzer.

    See

    https://github.com/flowr-analysis/flowr/wiki/Analyzer

    Example: Let's create an analyzer for a single R script file:

    const analyzer = new FlowrAnalyzerBuilder()
                         .setParser(new TreeSitterExecutor())
                         .buildSync()
                         .addRequest('file:///path/to/script.R')

    If you now want to get the dataflow information for the file, you can do this:

    const dfInfo = await analyzer.dataflow();
    console.log(dfInfo);

    • new FlowrAnalyzerBuilder(withDefaultPlugins?: boolean): FlowrAnalyzerBuilder

      Creates a new builder for the FlowrAnalyzer. By default, the standard set of plugins as returned by FlowrConfig#defaultPlugins are registered.

      Parameters

      • withDefaultPlugins: boolean = true

        Whether to register the default plugins upon creation. Default is true.

      Returns FlowrAnalyzerBuilder

      See

      • FlowrDefaultPlugins - for the default plugin set.
      • FlowrAnalyzerBuilder#registerPlugins - to add more plugins.
      • FlowrAnalyzerBuilder#unregisterPlugins - to remove plugins.

      Apply an amendment to the configuration the builder currently holds. This is mostly intended for more complex logic to transform the config. Please consider using FlowrAnalyzerBuilder.configure to set/amend individual values Per default, the value returned by FlowrConfig.default is used.

    build

    • build(): Promise<FlowrAnalyzer<KnownParser>>

      Create the FlowrAnalyzer instance using the given information. Please note that the only reason this is async is that if no parser is set, we need to retrieve the default engine instance which is an async operation. If you have already initialized the engine (e.g., with TreeSitterExecutor#initTreeSitter), you can use the synchronous version FlowrAnalyzerBuilder#buildSync instead.

      Returns Promise<FlowrAnalyzer<KnownParser>>

      • Defined in src/project/flowr-analyzer-builder.ts:181

    buildSync

    • buildSync(): FlowrAnalyzer

      Synchronous version of FlowrAnalyzerBuilder#build, please only use this if you have set the parser using FlowrAnalyzerBuilder#setParser before, otherwise an error will be thrown.

      Returns FlowrAnalyzer

          key: K,
          value: ConfigValueAt<K>,

      Set a specific value in the configuration used by the resulting analyzer.

      Besides the configuration's own paths this takes an EngineConfigPath, so an engine option that lives in an array entry is reachable the same way as everything else:
